quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January-December 2025) results: net sales JPY 4,624,727 million (up 2.5%), a record for the second consecutive year; gross profit JPY 2,162.0 billion (up 0.9%) with the gross margin down 0.8 points to 46.7%; operating profit JPY 455.4 billion (up 62.8%), an operating margin of 9.8%, helped by overseas restructuring effects and cost control and by the absence of the prior-year Medical goodwill impairment; net income attributable to Canon shareholders JPY 332.1 billion (up 107.5%). Management states printing fell as customers in Europe and the US kept postponing investment, medical was firm in the US and emerging markets, and network cameras and cameras capturing video demand sold well. Overseas sales were 79.2% of consolidated net sales. Sales by segment: Printing JPY 2,494,398 million, Medical JPY 580,622 million, Imaging JPY 1,054,900 million, Industrial JPY 361,128 million.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 4,624,727 million (+2.5%); operating profit JPY 455.4 billion (+62.8%); operating margin 9.8%; net income JPY 332.1 billion (+107.5%)

quarterly_data.signal: Industrial Business Unit FY2025: sales JPY 361.1 billion (up 2.7%; optical equipment JPY 256.3 billion, up 1.2%; industrial equipment JPY 101.6 billion, up 9.7%), pre-tax profit JPY 64.8 billion (down 7.9%) partly on product mix. Management states that in semiconductor lithography equipment demand for memory and power semiconductors was weak while AI-related demand stayed high, and unit sales of its advanced back-end (packaging) lithography tools, which it describes as the industry standard, exceeded the prior year; FPD lithography unit sales also rose as panel makers added investment for higher-function smartphone panels. Management describes the semiconductor equipment market as one where the recovery of memory demand for smartphones and PCs was delayed and power-semiconductor investment was postponed, but AI-related demand expanded. Industrial production in FY2025 was JPY 346,610 million (94.1% of the prior year); Canon discloses no orders because it mainly builds to forecast.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial sales JPY 361.1 billion (+2.7%); pre-tax profit JPY 64.8 billion (-7.9%); optical equipment JPY 256.3 billion (+1.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: New five-year plan Global Excellent Corporation Plan Phase VII (2026-2030) targets: net sales JPY 5 trillion in 2028 and JPY 5.6 trillion in 2030 (FY2025 actual JPY 4.6247 trillion), operating margin 12.0% in 2028 and 15.0% in 2030 (FY2025 9.8%), and ROE 12.0% and 15.0% (FY2025 9.7%). Management states Phase VI reached its 2025 sales target of JPY 4.5 trillion a year early but missed its 12% operating margin target because of rising labour costs, inflation and tariffs; Phase VII prioritises the faster-growing Medical and Industrial groups, structural reforms of sales (Europe by 2028), production and Medical (Canon Medical Systems to be merged into Canon in 2026), a full-scale entry into space business and AI-platform solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: 2028 targets: net sales JPY 5 trillion, operating margin 12.0%, ROE 12.0%; 2030 targets: net sales JPY 5.6 trillion, operating margin 15.0%, ROE 15.0%

quarterly_data.signal: Management's Industrial Group strategy: it sees the semiconductor market, despite ups and downs, driven by AI demand with large investment plans under way in many countries, and display investment recovering toward OLED for automotive, IT and large TVs. In semiconductor lithography Canon will raise the precision and productivity of its i-line and KrF tools to gain share and expand the business by entering ArF lithography; for nanoimprint lithography it will build an ecosystem through collaboration with strategic customers and partners and grow the patterning tools and the wafer planarization tools (an application of the same technology already commercialised) into a core business; in deposition it aims to put the new Adastra platform on track. For the rapidly expanding package substrate market it will cement its overwhelming market share in i-line lithography tools and launch new substrate-processing equipment. It also aims to expand beyond its current manufacturing equipment, including through M&A.

R&D: FY2025 group R&D expenses JPY 339,288 million, of which Industrial Business Unit JPY 32,286 million. Industrial R&D results named: the nanoimprint semiconductor manufacturing tool FPA-1200NZ2C, which forms fine circuit patterns by stamping and needs no wavelength-driven shrink, cutting power use; the i-line stepper FPA-3030i6 with a new high-transmittance, high-durability projection lens for power and green devices; and the FPD lithography tool MPAsp-E1003H for Gen 6 glass substrates, using Gen 8 projection optics that expose a 65-inch panel in one shot and widen the exposure field about 1.2 times.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 339,288 million; Industrial R&D JPY 32,286 million

quarterly_data.signal: Capex: FY2025 capital expenditure JPY 211,673 million (Industrial Business Unit JPY 14,137 million, expanding production equipment); purchases of fixed assets rose to JPY 262.2 billion, due in part to investment in the new semiconductor manufacturing equipment plant newly built at the Utsunomiya Office. Capex plan for 2026 (new construction and expansion) JPY 230,000 million, of which Industrial Business Unit JPY 20,600 million (production equipment expansion); management keeps total capex within depreciation.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex JPY 211,673 million; 2026 capex plan JPY 230,000 million (Industrial JPY 20,600 million)
